  PAGER=cat git stash drop

- **9g — Corrupted Rebase State Recovery:** If `git rebase --continue/--abort` fails with `warning: could not read '.git/rebase-merge/head-name'`: diagnose with `Test-Path ".git/rebase-merge"` / `Get-ChildItem ".git/rebase-merge"`; verify staged work via `PAGER=cat git diff --cached`; `Remove-Item ".git/rebase-merge" -Recurse -Force`; verify `PAGER=cat git status`; then commit normally (not `rebase --continue`).
- **9h — Pre-Existing Staged Content Handling:** Run `git diff --cached --stat`; if non-empty: present to user with warning, unstage if unrelated with `git reset HEAD -- .`, re-verify with `git diff --cached`, stage only intended files. (Only unstages; does not discard working-tree changes.)

- **9j — Post-Commit Verification:** After each commit, verify file set with `git show --name-only HEAD` (NOT `--stat`, which truncates long paths with `.../` and breaks grep/Select-String). Verify: (1) file set correct, (2) count matches expected, (3) no unintended files (no `.orig`, `.bak`, `.rej`, IDE artifacts). If wrong, diagnose via `git diff HEAD~1..HEAD` and correct before the next commit.

**Step 11 — Logic-Documentation Compass:** commit history visualized as compass — North: architectural/schema; East: logic/feature; West: testing/verification; South: documentation/refinement. No "spinning" (mixing logic and docs in one commit). **External Tool Asset Granularity:** for Postman/Insomnia/DBeaver assets, separate Environments / Collections / Data Tables; never one generic `test(tooling)` commit if purposes differ.

**Step 12 — Source Logic & Generated Files:** 11a — never manually edit generated files; update the source (templates/scripts/CI). 11b — detect generation (`<!-- AUTO-GENERATED -->`, build scripts, CI), locate source, document sync requirements in messages (e.g. "Run `npm run build` to regenerate"). 11c — CI/CD-managed files excluded from manual edits; maintain explicit exclusion list; verify with `git diff --cached` before committing.

**Step 13 — Intermediate State Synthesis:** For interleaved changes / 50+ line reorders / failed `git add -p` splits:
- Preferred scripted fallback (no working-tree mutation): `stage-file-excluding-lines.py --file <f> --exclude "<unwanted-line>"` → commit → `git add <f>` picks up remaining deltas.
- Fallback manual de-construction: edit to match atomic goal before staging, stage/commit, iterate until clean.
- Formatter-mixed files: delegate to [`separate-content-from-formatting-commits`](../separate-content-from-formatting-commits/SKILL.md).
- HEAD-Synthesis staging: `stage-head-synthesize.py --file <f> --replace "old|new"` reads `HEAD:<f>`, writes a blob, stages via `git update-index --cacheinfo`; working tree untouched.
- Sibling scripts listed: `agents-md-stage-row.py` (HEAD + one new row), `stage-file-excluding-lines.py` (working tree minus lines), `stage-head-synthesize.py` (HEAD + substitutions), `stage-hunk-from-diff.py` (selective hunks).

**Step 14 — User-Requested Coupling:** warn first ("This coupling technically violates Rule [X] because [reason]"), accept only on explicit re-confirmation, document deviation rationale in the body.

**Step 15 — Push Protocol:** do NOT `git push` unless explicitly requested; after commits OFFER to push and wait for explicit "yes"/command; always `git status` before push; never assume default branch — discover via `git branch -r`.

**Step 16 — Guardrail Against Predictive Planning:** never pre-commit in a plan to future content; commit construction is real-time analysis; plans are protocol roadmaps only.

**Cleanup protocols near the end / tail:**
- Preview file deletion only after all commits verified (2d.2, see item 3).
- Safety-stash release only at end-of-session, verified-then-dropped with explicit user authorization (2h, see item 6).

## 2. Commit message rules / format / templates

**Step 9 — Commit Message Quality Standards** (table, lines 1179–1187). Every message MUST satisfy:

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Specificity | Avoid generic titles (e.g. `add linux, macos, and windows gitignore rules`, not `os-specific`) |
| Anti-Repetition | Body MUST NOT merely rephrase the title |
| Context Enrichment | Explain the "Why", especially architectural/security decisions |
| Atomic Rationale | Body MUST state WHY these changes are grouped; explain functional coupling of multiple files |
| Constraint Documentation | Mention constraints/external dependencies influencing grouping |
| Contextual Accuracy | Precise terms (e.g. "Supabase project-specific" not generic "project-specific") |
| Body/Diff Congruence | Body MUST be a complete accurate summary of ALL staged hunks; discrepancy → immediate corrected preview |

## 6. Single-commit vs multi-commit sequences (safety stash applicability)

- **§2h — Pre-Execution Safety Stash is "Mandatory for ≥ 2 Commits."** It applies "before executing the first commit of any sequence of two or more commits (including any batch governed by §2g)". It captures an **apply-not-pop** snapshot of the full working-tree state (tracked modifications, staged hunks, AND untracked files), re-applies immediately, and persists across the sequence, verified-then-dropped only at end-of-session.
- **A 1-commit plan does NOT require the safety stash** (the mandate threshold is ≥2). Corroborating scope exclusions in "When to Apply": a "simple single-file, single-concern commit with no mixed changes (a lightweight commit suffices without the full protocol)".
- Three-phase protocol delegated to [`git-pre-execution-safety-stash`](../git-pre-execution-safety-stash/SKILL.md):
  - **Phase 1 — Snapshot:** classify pre-existing stashes via `git-stash-triage`; `git stash push -u -m "safety: ..."`; immediately `git stash apply` (NEVER `pop`); verify parity. If apply fails due to live-editor conflicts, do NOT retry — use the skill's Phase 1g "Selective File Extraction from Stash" recovery.
  - **Phase 2 — Hold:** never drop/pop/clear the `safety:` entry mid-sequence; re-verify presence at batch boundaries.
  - **Phase 3 — Verify-and-Release:** after final commit, `git stash apply` again, confirm clean no-op vs HEAD, then ask user explicitly before `git stash drop` (per `git-operation-rules.md` §5).
- Backing rule citations: `ai-agent-rules/git-atomic-commit-construction-rules.md` §3.3 (multi-commit safety stash), §3.2 (batch authorization), §3.1 (interleaving mandate), §4.3 (sidecar cleanup).
